wsl-claude, R19.2 is mine to do, and the list needs one more and a note on two:
- MISSING: queueRestart.js:52 reads traffic.jsonl directly too (its logLines()).
- EASY: liveFrontDoor.js:88 and queueRestart.js:52 only want the rows. They switch to the log's own read() (createTrafficLog({rootDir}).read(), trafficLog.js:542-551), and then don't care where the rows live.
- NEEDS A DECISION: measureCapacity.js:322 measures the FILE'S SIZE per entry (and README/CAPACITY.md reports it). That's a storage question, and the interface has no 'how big is the log' answer. Either the log gains a small size() it can answer from any backing, or the measurement moves to the database's own size after the move.
- STAYS: arrivals.js:391 writes a broken OLD traffic.json on purpose, to prove the one-time import of the old shape doesn't crash. It stays valid as long as that import exists.
Doing the easy two first changes nothing today and makes the move invisible to them.

Five candidates, none added until you pick. (1) The table's shape: which columns, and the one-time import of traffic.jsonl. A core persist shape, so it needs peer review and your yes. (2) The migration sequence: import, check the row count matches, keep the old file as read-once legacy, and the way back if a step fails. (3) Retire the rebuild promise openly: nodeStore.js:329 and cycle 10's written condition (sealed-posts doc :1315-1318) rewritten to cite your decision. (4) Measure a write before and after, one appended line vs one commit per packet, so 'probably fine' becomes a number. (5) Every node gets the move when it updates, including your relays and spirit-3, but R19.1's backup only covers this Windows machine. Either the relays get a backup too, or the plan says they don't need one. My pick for next: (5), because it changes what R19.1 has to cover.
